gate_type: IMPLEMENTATION gate — Single Simulation System Consolidation + Shared VF Shell. Gate verdict reached in this execution: BLOCKED FOR SA (audit-level blocker on one competing authority).

objective: Finish the architectural recovery so the repository reflects ONE Virtual Factory simulation system (one active RuntimeSession per user-selectable Workspace; domain engines subordinate; no hidden legacy authority; no legacy runtime fallback behind any active product route), audit and fix the TIPA scenario attempt-binding seam, implement the bounded shared-shell convergence authorized by the R4 UI audit (I1/I3/I4/I5/I6), and preserve all R1-R4 ASSY parity. Report READY only if every competing authority can be de-authorized without losing proven capability and without product-surface expansion.
explicit_non_objectives: No SH-WTP functional/whole-plant expansion (I2 dedicated SH-WTP process page NOT authorized)
No ASSY visual simplification or AssyLineRuntime rewrite
No deletion of proven domain capability without replacement/equivalence proof
forbidden_actions: Implement a partial consolidation that leaves an unreviewable half-migrated product path
Register a new user-selectable workspace or otherwise change the product surface without SA authorization
Delete or deprecate a proven capability that has no canonical equivalent
Expose executable source paths in this gate (no src/ or tests/ changes were made)
stop_conditions: A competing runtime/engine authority must remain an active product authority
De-authorizing a competing authority would lose a proven capability that has no canonical equivalent
Consolidating the competing authority requires a product-surface decision (new/registered workspace, selector change) beyond a bounded R5 correction
Scenario attempt binding requires broad generic lifecycle redesign
Consolidation would require rewriting AssyLineRuntime or SH-WTP domain semantics
SH-WTP expansion would become necessary to complete consolidation

acceptance_criteria.description: Repo-native inventory of every runtime/session/engine/controller construction site with a four-way classification (execution kernel/domain library; test/reference only; deprecate/remove active product reachability; delete only if proven redundant)

Product-path construction proof: canonical routes create exactly one session per workspace with one TIPA federation and six runtimes, and the non-canonical authorities that remain reachable are identified with hard evidence
Blocker analysis: the remaining competing authority cannot be de-authorized in R5 without capability loss or an unauthorized product-surface change, with concrete options for the SA
